answer: Compared like with like: modeled drive time (nearest firehouse by posted-speed drive time, 103k street-segment midpoints, median per MODZCTA area) vs FDNY median TRAVEL time (not response time, which adds turnout) for 2025 valid structural-fire records. Of 177 areas, 167 have >=20 incidents. The model is far too fast: median 1.53 min vs 3.85 observed, bias -2.2 min, MAE 2.2 min, RMSE 2.3, r=0.48, only 5/167 areas within 1 minute. Against full response time the gap widens (bias -2.9 min, 0 areas within 1 min). The model ranks areas only weakly and is not usable as a prediction of actual FDNY times; it is a free-flow lower bound.
traps_or_caveats: response_vs_travel: asked for 'response time'; modeled time is driving only, so the headline compares to incident_travel_tm_seconds_qy. Response time (includes turnout) shown only as secondary.
valid_flag: only valid_incident_rspns_time_indc='Y' records, structural fires, 2025.

zip_geography: dispatch postal ZIPs mapped to MODZCTA via member-ZIP list; 206 incidents unmatched and not scored: ZIP 11249 (94, likely a Williamsburg ZIP missing from the MODZCTA member list), null ZIP (110), 10151 and 10178 (1 each). Not silently dropped but not recovered.

Observed area values are incident-weighted means of postal-ZIP medians (approximation of a pooled median); the model value is a median over street midpoints, so it weights streets, not fires, equally.

Model assumes posted speed, no traffic/siren effects, no dispatch delays, nearest house always available and first-due; real units are often not the nearest, or busy, and real speeds are below posted. Large systematic underestimate is expected and is a limit of the model, not a finding about FDNY performance.

Marine units excluded from firehouse set in the main run (all-firehouses sensitivity gives same stats). Firehouse list includes battalion/division/borough command co-located facilities; counted as stations.
